reason: The primary CIF is valid and primitive: it parses as P1 with 20 fully occupied sites, exact K4MgCu3F12 (Z = 1), a = b = c = 7.397413 angstrom, V = 404.7992 angstrom^3, and no smaller cell or hidden symmetry through 0.1 angstrom tolerance. Its periodic chemistry has no gross veto (Mg-F 2.066-2.547 angstrom for the first six, shortest Cu-F 2.026 angstrom, shortest F-F 2.197 angstrom), and all important reflections have excellent primitive-cubic line indexing. Exact atom-coordinate recovery is nevertheless not established. The final P1 search uses 12 independent F sites, i.e. 36 positional variables, against only 40 powder-overlapped cubic shell intensities. The reported 0.9893 integrated-intensity correlation therefore masks substantial, over-parameterized discrepancies: an independent comparison using the same profile shape gives a unit-weight whole-profile residual of 9.50% for selected.cif (12.22% for alternative-1.cif), versus a 3.59% Pawley-like free-shell lower bound; the primary residual RMS is 0.402 against off-peak noise of 0.108, including an approximately 12.5-unit underfit of strong shell n = 12. The trace also shows many materially different F basins from independent starts rather than coordinate convergence, while the final F-F constraint was applied only by local refinement to two chosen basins. Formal charge assignment and plausible distances do not resolve that diffraction-relevant fluorine ordering ambiguity. Another solution attempt is therefore likely to add a materially different viable ordered realization.
